claim: A field experiment was conducted in the dry season of 2017 (January-May) at the International Rice Research Institute in Los Baños, Laguna, Philippines.
source: We conducted a field experiment in the dry season of 2017 (January-May) at the International Rice Research Institute in Los Baños, Laguna, Philippines.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the location and timing of the field experiment.

claim: Three replicates of each accession were planted separately in a normal wet paddy field and a field with moderate salinity stress (6 dSm–1).
source: Three replicates of each accession were planted separately in a normal wet paddy field as well as a similar field in which plants were exposed to moderate salinity stress (salt levels maintained at 6 dSm–1) maintained until maturity.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental design with specific salt concentration.

claim: Average fecundity was significantly lower in the saline field than in normal conditions (two-tailed paired t-test p=1.658 x 10–8).
source: Average fecundity was significantly lower in the saline field than in normal conditions (Figure 1a; two-tailed paired t-test p=1.658 x 10–8)
evidence: Statistical test results and figure reference support this finding.

claim: Most genotypes (n=94) had significantly lower fecundity in the saline field (one-sample proportion test p=3.639 x 10–7).
source: with most of genotypes having significantly lower fecundity in the saline field (n=94; one-sample proportion test p=3.639 x 10–7).
evidence: Statistical test results support this claim about genotype-specific responses.

claim: mRNA levels were measured in leaf blades from 780 plants (130 accessions in triplicates for each environment) via 3'-end-biased mRNA sequencing.
source: To examine gene expression in the field, mRNA levels were measured in leaf blades from 780 plants (130 accessions in triplicates for each environment) via 3'-end-biased mRNA sequencing (Meyer et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript describes the methodology and cites the sequencing protocol.

claim: Leaf blades were sampled 38 days after sowing (DAS), corresponding to 7 days of plants being exposed to stress in the saline field.
source: Leaf blades were sampled 38 days after sowing (DAS), corresponding to 7 days of plants being exposed to stress in the saline field.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the timing of tissue sampling.

claim: At a conservative false discovery rate (FDR) of 0.001, all but 3 transcripts displayed a significant genotype effect.
source: At a conservative false discovery rate (FDR) of 0.001, all but 3 transcripts displayed a significant genotype effect, indicating that expression levels of most transcripts are heritable.
evidence: Statistical analysis results are directly stated.

claim: The median broad-sense heritability (H2) of gene expression levels was 0.53 (range of 0.012–0.987).
source: This effect of genotype is reflected in the broad-sense heritability (H2) distribution of gene expression levels (Figure 1b), which had a median value H2=0.53 (range of 0.012–0.987; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Heritability values are provided with figure reference.

claim: 16,371 transcripts had a significant G×E term, indicating that for many transcripts, genotypes showed heritably different levels of expression in different environments.
source: In addition to the high levels of heritability, 16,371 transcripts had a significant G×E term, indicating that for many transcripts, genotypes showed heritably different levels of expression in different environments.
evidence: Statistical results from ANOVA are directly stated.

claim: There was no evidence of genotype-dependent plasticity in fitness (G×E for fitness p=0.49).
source: Although we see a widespread heritable plastic response in gene expression, we found no evidence of genotype-dependent plasticity in fitness (G×E for fitness p=0.49; Figure 1a)
evidence: Statistical test result is provided with figure reference.

claim: Only 254 transcripts showed significant variation due to environment (E), indicating genotype-independent plasticity in gene expression for only a small fraction of genes.
source: Furthermore, only a relatively small number of transcripts (254) showed significant variation due to E, indicating genotype-independent plasticity in gene expression for only a small fraction of genes.
evidence: The number of transcripts with environment effects is stated.

claim: Most transcripts were nearly neutral (|S|<0.1) in both the normal and saline environments.
source: Most transcripts were (nearly) neutral (|S|<0.1) in both the normal and saline environments (Figure 1c).
evidence: Selection analysis results are stated with figure reference.

claim: In the normal environment, there was a general trend towards stronger positive (9654 transcripts with S>0) compared to negative (8,415 transcripts with S<0) selection on gene expression (Mann-Whitney U-test, normal: p=3.95 x 10–15).
source: Additionally, within the normal environment, there was a general trend towards stronger positive (9654 transcripts with S>0) compared to negative (8,415 transcripts with S<0) selection on gene expression, indicating that higher expression of transcribed genes is associated with greater fitness (Table 1, Mann-Whitney U-test, normal: p=3.95 x 10–15).
evidence: Statistical test results and transcript counts are provided.

claim: In the saline field, higher expression of most of the transcribed genes is associated with lower fitness (Mann-Whitney U-test, saline: p=0.0068).
source: In comparison, although the strength of positive directional selection was higher than that of negative directional selection in the saline field, higher expression of most of the transcribed genes is associated with lower fitness (Table 1, Mann-Whitney U-test, saline: p=0.0068).
evidence: Statistical test result is provided.

claim: Under normal conditions, 17 transcripts cleared the Bonferroni correction threshold, 13 of which were under positive directional selection.
source: Although no transcripts cleared the Bonferroni correction threshold in saline conditions, under normal conditions 17 transcripts cleared the threshold, 13 of which were under positive directional selection (Supplementary file 3).
evidence: Statistical significance results are stated.

claim: A high proportion of transcripts experienced stabilizing selection (C<0) in both normal and saline environments.
source: We also found that a high proportion of transcripts experienced stabilizing selection (C<0) in both normal and saline environments.
evidence: Selection analysis results are directly stated.

claim: Stabilizing selection was stronger than disruptive selection under normal conditions (Mann-Whitney U-test, normal: p<2.2 x 10–16).
source: This effect was pronounced under normal conditions, with the strength of stabilizing selection being stronger than that of disruptive selection (Table 1; Mann-Whitney U-test, normal: p<2.2 x 10–16).
evidence: Statistical test result is provided.

claim: In the saline environment, there was no detectable difference between the strength of stabilizing and disruptive selection (Mann-Whitney U-test, normal: p=0.514).
source: In contrast, within the saline environment, there was no detectable difference between the strength of stabilizing and disruptive selection (Mann-Whitney U-test, normal: p=0.514), due to a higher proportion of transcripts experiencing stronger disruptive selection.
evidence: Statistical test result is provided.

claim: Selection was stronger in the saline field compared to the normal wet paddy field for overall strength of directional selection (Mann-Whitney U-test, p=0.012).
source: Comparing the distribution of selection differentials between environmental conditions, we found that selection was stronger in the saline field compared to the normal wet paddy field (Table 1; Figure 1d and e). This was true for the overall strength of directional selection (Mann-Whitney U-test, p=0.012)
evidence: Statistical test result is provided with figure reference.

claim: Selection was stronger in the saline field for negative directional (p=8.27 × 10–6), stabilizing (p<2.2 x 10–16) and disruptive (p<2.2 x 10–16) selection, but not positive directional selection (p=0.735).
source: as well as for negative directional (p=8.27 × 10–6), stabilizing (p<2.2 x 10–16) and disruptive (p<2.2 x 10–16) selection, but not positive directional selection (p=0.735).
evidence: Multiple statistical test results are provided.

claim: 10.80% of the transcripts showed selection patterns consistent with conditional neutrality, while only 0.28% of transcripts showed antagonistic pleiotropy.
source: We found that 10.80% of the transcripts showed selection patterns consistent with CN, while only 0.28% of transcripts showed AP (Figure 1f; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: Percentages are stated with figure reference.

claim: The proportion of transcripts showing conditional neutrality was greater than expected by chance and greater than the proportion showing antagonistic pleiotropy (two-tailed proportion z-test p<2.2 x 10–16).
source: The proportion of transcripts showing CN was greater than expected by chance and greater than the proportion showing AP two-tailed proportion z-test p<2.2 x 10–16.
evidence: Statistical test result is provided.

claim: Among the 51 antagonistically pleiotropic transcripts, increased expression of 38 was beneficial only in normal conditions.
source: Among the 51 AP transcripts, increased expression of 38 was beneficial only in normal conditions (higher expression associated with higher fitness in normal conditions, but lower fitness under saline conditions).
evidence: The number of transcripts with specific selection patterns is stated.

claim: Gene ontology term analyses of the 38 antagonistically pleiotropic transcripts beneficial in normal conditions indicated that many of these genes were involved in photosynthesis and metabolic processes.
source: Gene ontology (GO) term analyses of these 38 transcripts indicated that many of these genes were involved in photosynthesis and metabolic processes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: GO analysis results are stated with figure reference.

claim: The finding that many antagonistically pleiotropic genes are involved in photosynthesis and metabolic processes is consistent with an observed reduction of photosynthesis in rice under salinity stress.
source: This is consistent with an observed reduction of photosynthesis in rice under salinity stress (Radanielson et al., 2018; Tsai et al., 2019).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies supporting this interpretation.

claim: SNPs regulating expression of two photosynthesis related antagonistically pleiotropic transcripts (PSAN and CRR7) were found only in the normal environment.
source: We found SNPs regulating expression of two photosynthesis related AP transcripts (PSAN and CRR7) only in the normal environment (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: eQTL analysis results are stated with figure reference.

claim: Among the 13 antagonistically pleiotropic transcripts beneficial only in the saline environment, a cyclophilin-encoding transcript (OsCYP2) was identified, which has been shown to confer salt tolerance in rice.
source: We further looked at the 13 AP transcripts that were beneficial only in the saline environment (Supplementary file 4). Although there was no significant GO enrichment for these transcripts, among them we identified a cyclophilin-encoding transcript (OsCYP2), which has been shown to confer salt tolerance in rice (Lee et al., 2015; Roy et al., 2022; Ruan et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript identifies a specific gene and cites prior studies on its function.

claim: No SNP was associated with the expression of OsCYP2 in either normal or saline conditions.
source: However, no SNP was associated with the expression of this gene in either normal or saline conditions.
evidence: eQTL analysis results are stated.

claim: 13 biological processes were under strong differential selection in normal conditions and 18 processes in saline conditions.
source: We identified 13 and 18 processes that were under strong differential selection in normal and saline conditions, respectively (Supplementary file 5; Figure 2a).
evidence: The number of processes under selection is stated with figure reference.

claim: Processes primarily involved in various aspects of growth and defense were under stronger selection in normal conditions.
source: Processes primarily involved in various aspects of growth and defense were under stronger selection in normal conditions
evidence: Selection analysis results on biological processes are stated.

claim: Processes associated with regulation of flowering, cell cycle control and reproduction showed stronger selection under saline conditions.
source: whereas processes associated with regulation of flowering, cell cycle control and reproduction showed stronger selection under saline conditions (Figure 2a).
evidence: Selection analysis results on biological processes are stated with figure reference.

claim: Salinity stress affects cell cycle regulation, leading to reduced growth and reproduction.
source: Aligned with this, our study also supports the notion that salinity stress affects cell cycle regulation, and leads to reduced growth and reproduction.
evidence: The manuscript interprets findings in context of prior knowledge.

claim: Over half of principal components (7 of 11 in normal and 7 of 12 in saline conditions) displayed opposite signs of direct and indirect responses to selection.
source: We found that over half of PCs (7 of 11 and 7 of 12 PCs in normal and saline conditions, respectively) displayed opposite signs of direct and indirect responses to selection (Supplementary file 7).
evidence: Analysis results on selection responses are stated.

claim: PCs enriched for metabolic pathways and biosynthesis of phenylpropanoids and secondary metabolites were under selection in the normal environment.
source: We found PCs enriched for metabolic pathways and biosynthesis of phenylpropanoids and secondary metabolites to be under selection in the normal environment (Figure 2a; Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Supplementary file 7).
evidence: Selection analysis results are stated with figure references.

claim: Circadian rhythm was found to be under positive directional selection, with an overall positive response to selection, in the saline environment.
source: Interestingly, circadian rhythm was found to be under positive directional selection, with an overall positive response to selection, in the saline environment (Figure 2a; Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Supplementary file 7).
evidence: Selection analysis results are stated with figure references.

claim: The finding that circadian rhythm is under positive directional selection in the saline environment is in alignment with the role of circadian clock genes in conferring salt tolerance.
source: This is in alignment with the role of circadian clock genes in conferring salt tolerance (Kim et al., 2013; Wei et al., 2021; Xu et al., 2022)
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies supporting this interpretation.

claim: More than 29,000 transcript pairs (involving 1742 unique transcripts) showed significantly different correlations between normal and saline conditions (FDR <5%).
source: We found that the correlation structure for gene expression was broadly similar across the 2.10 M unique transcript pairs, but >29,000 transcript pairs (involving 1742 unique transcripts) showed significantly different correlations between normal and saline conditions (FDR <5%) (Figure 3a; Supplementary file 8).
evidence: Decoherence analysis results are stated with figure reference.

claim: GO term enrichment analysis of transcripts showing decoherence highlighted important pathways related to plant responses and potentially tolerance to excess salt.
source: GO term enrichment analysis of the transcripts that show decoherence with significant pairs greater than the median (median significant pair per transcript = 12, n=853) highlighted important pathways related to plant responses and potentially tolerance to excess salt (Figure 3b).
evidence: GO enrichment analysis results are stated with figure reference.

claim: Circadian rhythm genes like OsPRR37 and GIGANTA (GI), which have been shown to confer salt tolerance in rice and Arabidopsis, differed significantly in their interactions between the two environments.
source: For instance, circadian rhythm genes like OsPRR37 and GIGANTA (GI), which have been shown to confer salt tolerance in rice and Arabidopsis (Kim et al., 2013; Wei et al., 2021), differed significantly in their interactions between the two environments.
evidence: Decoherence analysis results are stated with citations to prior functional studies.

claim: Three traits – leaf osmotic potential (LOP), chlorophyll a content (Chl_a), and flowering time (FT) – displayed different selection patterns in normal versus saline environments.
source: We identified three traits – leaf osmotic potential (LOP), chlorophyll a content (Chl_a), and flowering time (FT) – that displayed different selection patterns in normal versus saline environments (Figure 4; Supplementary file 9).
evidence: Selection analysis results on phenotypic traits are stated with figure reference.

claim: Leaf osmotic potential was under positive directional selection in the control environment but under stabilizing selection under saline conditions.
source: Leaf osmotic potential is a key trait associated with water transport in plants, and which decreases with increasing salinity, leading to low water uptake by the plant. This trait was under positive directional selection in the control environment but under stabilizing selection under saline conditions, which suggests that an optimal LOP is important under salt stress (Figure 4).
evidence: Selection analysis results are stated with figure reference and biological interpretation.

claim: Chlorophyll a content at the reproductive stage was under negative directional selection in saline conditions.
source: Furthermore, we found Chl_a content at the reproductive stage to be under negative directional selection in saline conditions.
evidence: Selection analysis results are stated.

claim: The reduction in chlorophyll a content is associated with increased survival and reproductive fitness under saline conditions.
source: Although ion toxicity has previously been shown to reduce chlorophyll content (Ashraf and Bhatti, 2000; Taïbi et al., 2016), our results showed that this reduction is associated with increased survival and reproductive fitness, consistent with the general trend for reduced photosynthesis under salinity stress.
evidence: The manuscript interprets findings with citations to prior studies.

claim: Flowering time was under positive directional selection (selection for later flowering) in normal conditions but under stabilizing selection in saline conditions.
source: We also found that FT was under positive directional selection (selection for later flowering) in normal conditions but under stabilizing selection in saline conditions (Figure 4).
evidence: Selection analysis results are stated with figure reference.

claim: Flowering time was significantly reduced under saline conditions (two-tailed paired t-test p=0.0012).
source: Moreover, FT was significantly reduced under saline conditions (two-tailed paired t-test p=0.0012; Figure 4—figure supplement 2)
evidence: Statistical test result is provided with figure reference.

claim: cis- and trans-eQTLs (FDR <0.001) were identified regulating expression of 3065 and 3277 genes in normal and salinity stress conditions, respectively.
source: We identified cis- and trans-eQTLs (FDR <0.001) regulating expression of 3065 and 3277 genes in normal and salinity stress conditions, respectively (Supplementary file 10).
evidence: eQTL analysis results are stated.

claim: The median number of cis- and trans-eQTLs regulating the expression of a gene were similar between environments (median eQTL per gene cis-normal=14, cis-saline=13, trans-normal=5, trans-saline=4).
source: The median number of cis- and trans-eQTLs regulating the expression of a gene were similar between environments (median eQTL per gene cis-normal=14, cis-saline=13, trans-normal=5, trans-saline=4).
evidence: eQTL analysis results are stated.

claim: 49.64% (29,623 of a total 59,669) of cis-eQTLs were common in both environments, as compared to 18.62% (25,528 of a total 137,100) of trans-eQTLs.
source: We observed that 49.64% (29,623 of a total 59,669) of cis-eQTLs were common in both environments, as compared to 18.62% (25,528 of a total 137,100) of trans-eQTLs
evidence: eQTL overlap analysis results are stated.

claim: trans-eQTLs explain more variation in transcript abundance as compared to cis-eQTLs in both environments (two-tailed t-test p<10–16; mean effect size: cis-normal=0.77, trans-normal=1.04, cis-saline=0.80, trans-saline=1.08).
source: Moreover, comparing the effect sizes of the two categories of eQTLs, we found that trans-eQTLs explain more variation in transcript abundance as compared to cis-eQTLs in both environments (two-tailed t-test p<10–16; mean effect size: cis-normal=0.77, trans-normal=1.04, cis-saline=0.80, trans-saline=1.08).
evidence: Statistical test results comparing effect sizes are provided.

claim: At FDR of 0.05, cis-eQTLs constituted merely 0.28% (142 of 50718) of the total identified G×eQTLs.
source: We tested this explicitly by identifying loci showing gene-environment interaction (G×eQTL) and found that at FDR of 0.05, cis-eQTLs constituted merely 0.28% (142 of 50718) of the total identified G×eQTLs.
evidence: G×eQTL analysis results are stated.

claim: 11 trans-eQTL hotspots (number of unique genes >30) were identified in saline conditions, but none in normal conditions.
source: Through this approach, we identified 11 trans-eQTL hotspots (number of unique genes >30) in saline conditions, but none in normal conditions (Figure 5—figure supplement 1; Supplementary file 11).
evidence: eQTL hotspot analysis results are stated with figure reference.

claim: One hotspot, Chr7: 25.9–26.0 Mb, influenced the expression of 191 genes and contains the gene OsFLP, a R2R3 myb-like transcription factor that regulates stomatal development.
source: Interestingly, one of the hotspots, Chr7: 25.9–26.0 Mb, influenced the expression of a disproportionately high number of genes (191 genes) and contains the gene OsFLP, a R2R3 myb-like transcription factor that regulates stomatal development (Wu et al., 2019).
evidence: eQTL hotspot analysis results are stated with citation to gene function.

claim: OsFLP has recently been associated with salt tolerance in rice.
source: OsFLP has recently been associated with salt tolerance in rice (Qu et al., 2022).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study on gene function.

claim: More than half of genes with both cis and trans regulation appear to have a reinforcing rather than a compensatory pattern (two-tailed proportion z-test p=1.65 x 10–11).
source: Contrary to this expectation, we found that more than half genes appear to have a reinforcing (cis and trans effect in the same direction) rather than a compensatory pattern (two-tailed proportion z-test p=1.65 x 10–11; Figure 5a; Supplementary file 12).
evidence: Statistical test result is provided with figure reference.

claim: Among the 524 cis-trans co-occurring genes in saline conditions, 317 were reinforcing (~60.5%) and 207 were compensatory (39.5%).
source: Among the 524 cis-trans co-occurring genes in saline conditions, 317 were reinforcing (~60.5%) and 207 were compensatory (39.5%).
evidence: The numbers of genes in each category are stated.

claim: Genes under cis-trans reinforcement showed significantly higher inter-varietal expression variation as compared to genes under cis-trans compensation in saline conditions (Mann-Whitney U-test=0.002; mean-inter-varietal expression variation compensating = 1.12, reinforcing = 1.27).
source: Supporting our hypothesis, we found significantly higher inter-varietal expression variation for genes under cis-trans reinforcement in saline (Figure 5b; Mann-Whitney U-test=0.002; mean-inter-varietal expression variation compensating = 1.12, reinforcing = 1.27)
evidence: Statistical test result is provided with figure reference.

claim: Estimated linkage disequilibrium between all pairs of cis- and trans-regulatory variants for the identified compensating and reinforcing genes was significantly higher as compared to the background LD (mean r2 compensating: 0.33, reinforcing: 0.36, background = 0.056; two-tailed permutation test p=0.0019).
source: This was indeed the case: estimated LD between all pairs of cis- and trans-regulatory variants for the identified compensating and reinforcing genes was significantly higher as compared to the background LD (mean r2 compensating: 0.33, reinforcing: 0.36, background = 0.056; two-tailed permutation test p=0.0019).
evidence: Statistical test result is provided.

claim: trans-eQTLs for both environments had been under strong purifying selection, with the site-frequency spectrum being significantly left-shifted compared to background SNPs (two-tailed t-test p<10–16; mean MAF background = 0.20, trans normal = 0.0936, trans saline = 0.0910).
source: We found that trans-eQTLs for both environments had been under strong purifying selection, with the SFS being significantly left-shifted compared to background SNPs (two-tailed t-test p<10–16; mean MAF background = 0.20, trans normal = 0.0936, trans saline = 0.0910).
evidence: Statistical test result is provided.

claim: trans-eQTLs regulating multiple genes showed stronger purifying selection than those regulating single genes (two-tailed t-test p<10–16; normal mean MAF in unique trans-eQTLs=0.099, multiple trans-eQTL=0.073; saline mean MAF in unique trans-eQTLs=0.097, multiple trans-eQTL=0.071).
source: Not surprisingly, given their highly pleiotropic nature, this effect was more pronounced for trans-eQTLs regulating multiple genes (two-tailed t-test p<10–16; normal mean MAF in unique trans-eQTLs=0.099, multiple trans-eQTL=0.073; saline mean MAF in unique trans-eQTLs=0.097, multiple trans-eQTL=0.071).
evidence: Statistical test result is provided.

claim: cis-eQTLs in both normal and saline conditions had potentially been under balancing selection with the site-frequency spectrum being significantly right-shifted for cis-eQTLs relative to background SNPs (two-tailed t-test p<10–16; mean MAF background = 0.20, cis normal = 0.238, cis saline = 0.237).
source: In contrast to trans-eQTLs, we found that cis-eQTLs in both normal and saline conditions had potentially been under balancing selection (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 3) with the SFS being significantly right-shifted for cis-eQTLs relative to background SNPs (two-tailed t-test p<10–16; mean MAF background = 0.20, cis normal = 0.238, cis saline = 0.237).
evidence: Statistical test result is provided with figure reference.

claim: The estimated nucleotide diversity (π) for 100 kb regions flanking cis-eQTLs was significantly higher as compared to genome-wide 100 kb blocks (two-tailed t-test p<10–11; mean π background = 0.286, cis normal = 0.297, cis saline = 0.297).
source: Moreover, for both conditions, the estimated nucleotide diversity (π) for 100 kb regions flanking cis-eQTLs was also significantly higher as compared to genome-wide 100 kb blocks (two-tailed t-test p<10–11; mean π background = 0.286, cis normal = 0.297, cis saline = 0.297).
evidence: Statistical test result is provided.

claim: trans-eQTLs in saline conditions were under stronger purifying selection compared to normal conditions (two-tailed t-test p=0.017).
source: However, we did observe trans-eQTLs in saline conditions to be under stronger purifying selection (two-tailed t-test p=0.017).
evidence: Statistical test result is provided.

claim: Salinity stress induces increased selective pressure on gene expression.
source: We find that salinity stress induces increased selective pressure on gene expression.
evidence: This is a summary claim stated in the abstract and supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claim: trans-eQTLs rather than cis-eQTLs are primarily associated with rice's gene expression under salinity stress, potentially via a few master-regulators.
source: Further, we show that trans-eQTLs rather than cis-eQTLs are primarily associated with rice's gene expression under salinity stress, potentially via a few master-regulators.
evidence: This is a summary claim stated in the abstract and supported by eQTL analysis data.

claim: cis-trans reinforcement is more common than cis-trans compensation, which may be reflective of rice diversification subsequent to domestication.
source: Importantly, and contrary to the expectations, we find that cis-trans reinforcement is more common than cis-trans compensation which may be reflective of rice diversification subsequent to domestication.
evidence: This is a summary claim stated in the abstract and supported by cis-trans analysis data.

claim: Genetic fixation is the likely mechanism underlying cis-trans compensation/reinforcement.
source: We further identify genetic fixation as the likely mechanism underlying this compensation/reinforcement.
evidence: This is a summary claim stated in the abstract and supported by linkage disequilibrium analysis.

claim: cis-eQTLs are under balancing selection and trans-eQTLs are under purifying selection.
source: Additionally, we show that cis- and trans-eQTLs are under balancing and purifying selection, respectively, giving us insights into the evolutionary dynamics of gene expression variation.
evidence: This is a summary claim stated in the abstract and supported by site-frequency spectrum analysis.

claim: An estimated ~50–70% of crop yields are lost as a direct result of various abiotic stresses.
source: indeed, as a direct result of various abiotic stresses, an estimated ~50–70% of crop yields are lost (Francini and Sebastiani, 2019).
evidence: The manuscript cites a prior study for this estimate.

claim: Oryza sativa (Asian rice) is a salt-sensitive crop, facing significant yield loss due to soil salinity.
source: Oryza sativa (Asian rice) is one such salt-sensitive crop, facing significant yield loss due to soil salinity (Hussain et al., 2017; Melino and Tester, 2023).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies supporting this claim.

claim: Rice responds to salinity stress by adjusting physiological and biochemical processes involved in osmotic and ion homeostasis, nutritional balances and oxidative stress.
source: Rice responds to salinity stress by adjusting physiological and biochemical processes involved in osmotic and ion homeostasis, nutritional balances and oxidative stress (Castillo et al., 2007; Miller et al., 2010; Munns and Tester, 2008; Qin and Huang, 2020; Wang et al., 2012).
evidence: The manuscript cites multiple prior studies supporting this claim.

claim: The study builds on prior work that examined selection on gene expression in rice in response to normal and dry conditions.
source: This study builds on prior work by our group that examined selection on gene expression in rice in response to normal and dry conditions (Calic et al., 2022; Groen et al., 2020; Groen et al., 2021).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior studies by the same research group.

claim: The study used genomic, transcriptomic, and phenotypic datasets obtained from 130 diverse accessions of rice subjected to moderate levels of salinity stress.
source: Using genomic, transcriptomic, and phenotypic datasets obtained from 130 diverse accessions of rice subjected to moderate levels of salinity stress
evidence: The manuscript describes the study design.

claim: A total of 130 O. sativa ssp. indica (including indica and circum-aus groups) and 65 O. sativa ssp. japonica accessions were selected for the study.
source: For this study, a total of 130 O. sativa ssp. indica (including indica and circum-aus groups) and 65 O. sativa ssp. japonica (including circum-basmati, tropical japonica, and temperate japonica) accessions were selected, including traditional varieties/landraces and three additionally replicated salt-sensitive and -tolerant test varieties.
evidence: The manuscript describes the plant material used.

claim: The study focused analyses on O. sativa ssp. indica since it is the predominant global varietal group.
source: We focused our analyses on O. sativa ssp. indica since it is the predominant global varietal group (Supplementary file 13).
evidence: The manuscript explains the rationale for focusing on indica subspecies.

claim: The application of salt in the saline field started on January 19, 2017, when the plants were 31 days old.
source: The application of salt in site L5 started on January 19, 2017, when the plants were 31 days old.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental protocol.

claim: The salinity levels were maintained at 6 dSm–1 (considered mild to moderate salinity stress) until maturity.
source: The salinity levels were then maintained at 6 dSm–1 (considered mild to moderate salinity stress) until maturity.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental conditions.

claim: Raw sequence reads have been submitted to the SRA (BioProject PRJNA1010833).
source: Raw sequence reads have been submitted to the SRA (BioProject PRJNA1010833).
evidence: The manuscript states data availability.

claim: Genomes of 19 accessions were re-sequenced and submitted to the SRA (BioProject PRJNA1012700).
source: Further, genomes of 19 accessions were re-sequenced, and submitted to the SRA (BioProject PRJNA1012700), leading to a total of 125 accessions for which genomic data was available (Supplementary file 13).
evidence: The manuscript states data generation and availability.
